data.text: The historical evolution of augmented reality can be broadly divided into four overlapping phases from before the 1980s to the present. These phases progressed from early experimentation and basic research into the development of tools and widespread commercial applications.
points: The historical evolution of augmented reality can be broadly divided into four overlapping phases from before the 1980s to the present.
These phases progressed from early experimentation and basic research into the development of tools and widespread commercial applications.

data.text: Ivan Sutherland and Bob Sproull created the first computer-generated augmented reality prototype in 1968. This prototype used a head-mounted display and a tracking system to register head movements in three dimensions. The US Air Force super cockpit program produced technologies where pilots saw computer-generated imagery through a head-mounted display. These early experiments led to modern aircraft displays, virtual reality systems, and tracking hardware.

data.text: The basic research phase of augmented reality came after the experimentation phase and shaped the field during the 1990s, including the coining of the term "augmented reality" in 1992. Research during this phase focused on tracking techniques, head-mounted displays, and interaction methods. Early systems like Chameleon and NaviCam were true augmented reality applications and precursors to the kind of AR applications seen today.

data.text: Research in the mid-1990s focused on key technologies like tracking, display, and interaction, leading to developments in shared AR content, medical applications, and wearable computing. By 1997, computer vision and GPS were used to register 3D content in the real world. In the early 2000s, wearable AR systems were developed for various applications but remained bulky and difficult to use. Viewpoint tracking challenges were eventually addressed by systems like the AR Toolkit, which was later ported to mobile phones in 2004.
points: Mid-1990s research focused on key enabling technologies like tracking, display, and interaction.
This period saw the development of shared AR content, medical applications, and wearable computing using head-mounted displays.
By 1997, tracking techniques using computer vision markers and GPS were used to register 3D content.
In the early 2000s, wearable AR systems were developed for various applications but were bulky and difficult to use.
Viewpoint tracking was addressed by tools such as the AR Toolkit, which was later ported to mobile phones in 2004.

data.text: The commercial application phase of augmented reality began in October 2007 and moved from research laboratories to widely available technology by 2009, driven by new authoring tools, smartphones, and marketing campaigns. The launch of ARKit and ARCore in 2017 further stimulated growth by enabling developers to create complex applications. This phase is expected to continue growing as hardware improves and AI and computer vision technologies advance.
points: The commercial application phase of augmented reality began in October 2007 and made the technology popular among consumers.
In 2009, augmented reality moved from research laboratories to widely available commercial technology.
This shift was driven by Adobe Flash-based authoring tools, the start of the smartphone era, and global marketing campaigns.
The launch of ARKit and ARCore in 2017 stimulated growth by enabling developers to create more complex applications.
The commercial application phase is still ongoing and is expected to continue growing through improvements in hardware, AI, and computer vision.
